newsitem.title: EGYPT: EgyptAir boss revives convertible bond idea.
newsitem.headline: EgyptAir boss revives convertible bond idea.

text.p: The chairman of state airline EgyptAir said the airline could issue bonds convertible into equity up to the equivalent of 20 percent of the company's capital and assets, government newspapers said on Saturday.
But an airline official told Reuters that chairman Mohamed Fahim Rayyan was speaking only of one possibility and the company had no need or immediate plans to raise money in this way.

Rayyan, quoted in all government newspapers, said the bonds would have a nominal value of between $20,000 and $30,000 each and only Egyptian individuals would be eligible to buy them, up to a maximum of five bonds per individual.

"He said that studies were complete and that the issue would be done in agreement with a bank according to the market's capacity. He indicated that the yield would be higher than any other," said the newspaper Akhbar el-Yom.
EgyptAir, which is wholly state-owned, has capital of 56 million pounds ($16.5 million) and its assets have a book value of nine billion pounds ($2.65 billion), the chairman added.

EgyptAir's original plan was to raise money through bonds to help pay for its latest purchases of planes. But the airline official said it had found no problem raising the money by borrowing from banks and other institutions.
